lines.say: Three hundred fifty six dollars. That is how far Israel is from Germany.
GDP per person, in dollars, since 1980.
In 1980, the UAE is far ahead. Israel makes about sixty percent of a Brit.
Oil prices fall, and Saudi income halves in ten years.
In 2023, the war year, it falls back behind Germany.
Turkey keeps climbing, past eighteen thousand. Egypt and Jordan stay under six.
And in 2025, Israel reaches sixty thousand nine hundred.
Fair point: these are dollars, so a strong shekel lifts them.
Will Israel pass Germany again next year? Tell me in the comments.
So how big is the gap now?

caption_en:
It passed France, then Britain, then Germany for one year. Now look at the gap.

GDP per person, current US$, 2025 (IMF estimates):
Germany 61,255
Israel 60,899
UK 57,741
UAE 54,151
France 49,129
Saudi Arabia 35,370
Turkey 18,676
Lebanon 5,897
Jordan 5,169
Egypt 3,379
Syria: no IMF data after 2010

Israel passed France in 2016, the UK in 2019 and Germany in 2022 (54,474 vs 51,215), then fell back behind Germany in 2023. 1980: Israel 6,368, UK 10,692. Saudi Arabia fell from 19,543 (1980) to 8,562 (1990) as oil prices fell. The IMF projects Israel above Germany in 2026; projections can change.
These are dollar figures, so a strong shekel lifts Israel's numbers. Per person income is not the same as how well off every household is.

Source: IMF World Economic Outlook database (DataMapper), NGDPDPC, 1980 to 2025. The animation interpolates between years.

caption_he: תוצר לנפש, 2025 (קרן המטבע): גרמניה 61,255 דולר, ישראל 60,899. ישראל עקפה את צרפת ב 2016, את בריטניה ב 2019, ואת גרמניה ב 2022, לשנה אחת. הפער היום: 356 דולר. שקל חזק מגדיל את המספרים בדולרים.
